title: Hosted API surge readiness & safety-margin calculus — Q4 2026
body:
Purpose
This working doc captures a practical approach for hosted API surge readiness: how we calculate per-region safety margins (headroom), translate tokens/sec and QPS forecasts into GPU pool sizing, and operational mitigations for short-term flash events. Intended audience: infra on-call, capacity planning, release owners for hosted API.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Goal: default safety margin = 2.0x peak-to-P99 short-burst (configurable by region/tenant).
- Approach: model three surge scenarios (normal peak, flash-burst P99, redistributed-traffic-on-failover) and size pools by "sustained throughput per vGPU" estimates per model class.
- Quick recommendation: add ephemeral burst pool equal to 20% of steady-state pool in high-demand regions (us-west1, eu-west1) and increase cross-region routing weight tolerance to 30% for emergency failover.

Assumptions and definitions
- token = model token generated or consumed. We normalize on tokens/sec (tps) and QPS (requests/sec).
- Peak windows considered: 1m P90 (business-as-usual spike), 1m P99 (short flash), 10m sustained peak (longer event).
- "tokens_per_sec_per_gpu" is model-family dependent. We use conservative measured baselines from recent lab runs (see notes below).
- Safety margin (SM) = provisioning_factor * estimated_peak. Default provisioning_factor = 2.0 for hosted API public endpoints, 1.5 for private/dedicated customers unless contract specifies higher.

Measured baseline (reference numbers — lab-derived, conservative)
- Model class: small-chat (<=7B): ~80k tokens/sec per L4-equivalent instance under typical batching.
- Model class: medium-chat (~13B): ~18k tokens/sec per A10/A100-v2 40GB-equivalent instance.
- Model class: large-chat (70B): ~6k tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent.
- Embeddings-heavy (dense short outputs): ~150k tokens/sec per L4-equivalent.
Notes: these are ballpark figures for dimensioning only; final numbers must come from standardized bench runs in infra/benchmarks repo (PR referenced above).

Conversion examples (how we size)
- Formula: required_vgpus = ceil(peak_tokens_per_sec * safety_margin / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu)
- Example 1 (us-west1): observed 1m P99 = 250k tokens/sec for medium-chat workload. Safety margin = 2.0 -> target = 500k tps. Using 18k tps/gpu -> required_vgpus = ceil(500k / 18k) = 28 GPUs (round to next allocation bin = 32).
- Example 2 (eu-west1): embeddings peak = 400k tps P99. Safety margin 1.5 -> 600k tps target. Using 150k tps/L4 -> required_vgpus = ceil(600k / 150k) = 4 GPUs.

Regional surge scenarios (3 prioritized)
1) Flash Burst (marketing event / surprise traffic): 1-minute P99 spikes up to 3x baseline peak. Characteristics: short, high token emission, tolerant to small extra latency.
 - Mitigations: temporary increase in routing to H2S (burst pool), enable degraded response modes (token-capped responses), increase autoscale aggressiveness for 60s window.
2) Sustained Peak (10m+): sustained elevated throughput (e.g., seasonal demand).
 - Mitigations: scale steady-state pools, notify SRE, consider temporary reserved capacity purchase if predictable.
3) Regional Failover (region outage causes 40–80% of traffic to reroute to secondary): sudden step increase in destination region lasting 10–120 minutes.
 - Mitigations: pre-warm cross-region burst pools, policy-based rate-limits per-tenant to preserve fairness, automatic model-fallback to smaller variants for non-critical routes.

Operational controls and config recommendations
- Default safety margin per region: us-west1, eu-west1: 2.0x; ap-southeast1: 1.8x; others: 1.5x. Revisit quarterly.
- Burst pool: ephemeral GPUs labeled "burst-usw1" etc. Size = max(20% steady-state, min 8 GPUs). Rationale: avoids forcing over-provisioning of committed capacity while giving short-term relief.
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce cool-down to 30s for scale-up, keep scale-down conservative (10m) to avoid oscillation.
- Graceful degradation knobs: per-route token cap, reduce max streaming window, fallback to cached completions for repeated prompts.
- Routing policy: allow temporary >20% cross-region shift for 5–15 minutes; require manual review if >30% shift sustained beyond 30 minutes.

Per-tenant headroom model (sketch)
- For large customers we maintain per-tenant headroom percentage to guarantee SLAs. Default = 1.25x of tenant's max observed 30-day peak. This is separate from regional safety margin and should be treated as reservation with billing implications.

Short checklist for incident/on-call (quick runbook snippet)
- Step 0: Check traffic origin heatmap (console -> per-region QPS and tps).
- Step 1: If P99 > configured threshold, enable burst pool for affected region (infra tooling: /ops/burst-enable).
- Step 2: Flip per-route degradation for non-critical routes (console toggle).
- Step 3: Notify capacity channel (#infra-capacity) and post short blameless note with metrics and action.
- Step 4: If cross-region reroute > 30% for >30m, open ENGINFRA incident and consider temporary reserved capacity procurement.

Open questions / TODOs
- We need standardized bench numbers in infra/benchmarks for each model archetype and per-GPU type. Owner: @Carlos (ENGINFRA-492).
- Validate burst pool cold-start time on H100 vs A100 across cloud vendors; add 95% CI to planning docs. Owner: @Emily.
- Define billing treatment for ephemeral burst usage in hosted API (product decision). Owner: Product-hosted-api.

Appendix: example regional sizing table (working)
Columns: region | recent P99 tps (1m) | model class | tokens_per_sec_per_gpu | safety_margin | target_tps | required_gpus_raw | rounding_note
- us-west1 | 250k | medium-chat | 18k | 2.0 | 500k | 28 -> round to 32
- eu-west1 | 120k | medium-chat | 18k | 2.0 | 240k | 14 -> round to 16
- ap-southeast1 | 85k | small-chat | 80k | 1.8 | 153k | 2 -> round to 4
- us-east1 (embeddings) | 400k | embeddings | 150k | 1.5 | 600k | 4 -> round to 4

Notes and provenance
- This is an intentionally pragmatic document for planning discussions; numbers are approximate and flagged as "lab-derived" where relevant. Final commit to capacity should be gated on: (a) standardized benchmark runs, (b) simulated failover replay on past month traffic, (c) exec approval for any reserved purchases.
- Related: ENGINFRA-492 (bench numbers), infra PR 1183 (autoscaler tuning), doc/observability/route-heatmap (dashboard).

Contact and next steps

- Deliverable for next cycle: canonical sizing sheet in infra/capacity-runner with per-region inputs and simulation harness.

Working notes (notes-to-self style)
- consider gating model-fallback policy at route-level + tenant opt-out
- check cost impact if burst pools are H100-heavy (model-fallback to smaller model families can save both cost and headroom)
